pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

findingGroups.title: Invariant + regression coverage
findings: D2 watcher-affinity contract documented at basisset.h (class) and gaussianset.h/slaterset.h async entry points.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.

pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.

pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.

pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.

Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.

Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

findingGroups.title: Invariant + regression coverage
findings: D2 watcher-affinity contract documented at basisset.h (class) and gaussianset.h/slaterset.h async entry points.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

findingGroups.title: Invariant + regression coverage
findings: D2 watcher-affinity contract documented at basisset.h (class) and gaussianset.h/slaterset.h async entry points.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

findingGroups.title: Invariant + regression coverage
findings: D2 watcher-affinity contract documented at basisset.h (class) and gaussianset.h/slaterset.h async entry points.

tests: orbitalselectiontest 12/12 green; full ctest 44/44 under xvfb

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

findingGroups.title: Invariant + regression coverage
findings: D2 watcher-affinity contract documented at basisset.h (class) and gaussianset.h/slaterset.h async entry points.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

findingGroups.title: Invariant + regression coverage
findings: D2 watcher-affinity contract documented at basisset.h (class) and gaussianset.h/slaterset.h async entry points.

orbitalselectiontest gains 4 real-async-path slots: asyncLoadBasisIsGuiAffine (asserts basis->thread() == GUI), plus ORCA/fchk/molden end-to-end no-wedge tests. Molden exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no fixture).
tests: orbitalselectiontest 12/12 green; full ctest 44/44 under xvfb
