pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

findingGroups.title: Invariant + regression coverage
findings: D2 watcher-affinity contract documented at basisset.h (class) and gaussianset.h/slaterset.h async entry points.

orbitalselectiontest gains 4 real-async-path slots: asyncLoadBasisIsGuiAffine (asserts basis->thread() == GUI), plus ORCA/fchk/molden end-to-end no-wedge tests. Molden exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no fixture).
tests: orbitalselectiontest 12/12 green; full ctest 44/44 under xvfb

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

findingGroups.title: Invariant + regression coverage
findings: D2 watcher-affinity contract documented at basisset.h (class) and gaussianset.h/slaterset.h async entry points.

orbitalselectiontest gains 4 real-async-path slots: asyncLoadBasisIsGuiAffine (asserts basis->thread() == GUI), plus ORCA/fchk/molden end-to-end no-wedge tests. Molden exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no fixture).
tests: orbitalselectiontest 12/12 green; full ctest 44/44 under xvfb

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

findingGroups.title: Invariant + regression coverage
findings: D2 watcher-affinity contract documented at basisset.h (class) and gaussianset.h/slaterset.h async entry points.

orbitalselectiontest gains 4 real-async-path slots: asyncLoadBasisIsGuiAffine (asserts basis->thread() == GUI), plus ORCA/fchk/molden end-to-end no-wedge tests. Molden exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no fixture).
tests: orbitalselectiontest 12/12 green; full ctest 44/44 under xvfb

Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

findingGroups.title: Invariant + regression coverage
findings: D2 watcher-affinity contract documented at basisset.h (class) and gaussianset.h/slaterset.h async entry points.

orbitalselectiontest gains 4 real-async-path slots: asyncLoadBasisIsGuiAffine (asserts basis->thread() == GUI), plus ORCA/fchk/molden end-to-end no-wedge tests. Molden exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no fixture).
tests: orbitalselectiontest 12/12 green; full ctest 44/44 under xvfb

pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

findingGroups.title: Invariant + regression coverage
findings: D2 watcher-affinity contract documented at basisset.h (class) and gaussianset.h/slaterset.h async entry points.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.

pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

findings: D2 watcher-affinity contract documented at basisset.h (class) and gaussianset.h/slaterset.h async entry points.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.

pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.

pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

findingGroups.title: Invariant + regression coverage
findings: D2 watcher-affinity contract documented at basisset.h (class) and gaussianset.h/slaterset.h async entry points.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.

pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Per-item evidence for the verification contract, cross-checked against real artifacts:

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.

- Split parity: constructBasis/fillBasis in orbitalextension.cpp branch-by-branch matches the old BasisSetLoader::LoadBasisSet (fchk/gamess/gukout/aux/molden return the basis unconditionally; orca/out gated on orcaout.success(); fall-through yields null). gamout/gukout early paths use the raw fileName, as before. Null/empty-file and worker-fill-failure paths preserve the old null-return semantics.
- Thread affinity: loadBasis() constructs the basis at orbitalextension.cpp:1107 on the GUI thread before the QtConcurrent::run dispatch (:1109); loadBasis's only caller is setMolecule (GUI). Grep of `new GaussianSet|new SlaterSet` shows the only remaining construction sites are the synchronous GUI path (surfaceextension.cpp:266), the CLI (qube.cpp:97), and test mains — no off-GUI construction path remains. The worker only fills via reader constructors; it no longer deletes the basis (the GUI-thread continuation owns deletion on both stale-epoch and fill-failure paths).
- No leak/double-free: exactly one of {continuation delete on stale epoch, continuation delete on fill-failure, setMolecule teardown of m_basis} owns the pointer at a time; type pairing (aux→SlaterSet, all else→GaussianSet) is consistent.
- No new data race: the GUI never touches the new basis until the queued continuation runs (posted after the worker lambda returns; Qt's queued invocation is the sync point); m_basis is assigned only in the continuation; the watcher is first connected in calculateCube(), reachable only after m_basis is set. Epoch guard is byte-identical to the pre-diff shape.
- No lock-path changes: the diff touches no line of checkQueue/calculationComplete/m_runningMutex logic.
- Regression tests drive the real async path (setMolecule → real loadBasis → real QtConcurrent worker → queued continuation) and fail on the broken shape, matching the recorded red run. Molden coverage exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no .aux fixture, design D5).
- Reviewer verdict: OK with notes (no blocker, no major). Findings 1 (worker delete), 2 (test leaks), 4 (QTRY timeout) accepted and integrated; findings 3 (pre-existing leak) and 5 (double MatchBasisSet scan) deferred with reasons in the apply-log.

findingGroups.title: Watcher-affinity fix
findings: ORCA/Gaussian-fchk/Molden orbitals now render end-to-end; the queue drains without a document switch — the root cause was the basis (and its QFutureWatcher) constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread, so the cube 'finished()' callout was never delivered and the calculation queue wedged (m_runningMutex held forever). Fix: constructBasis runs on the GUI thread; fillBasis (stack readers) runs on the worker; the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis.
Verified by reviewer (OK with notes) + the recorded red run: reverting to construct-on-worker makes the affinity assert fail and the end-to-end test time out at ~89s, then both green with the fix.

findingGroups.title: Invariant + regression coverage
findings: D2 watcher-affinity contract documented at basisset.h (class) and gaussianset.h/slaterset.h async entry points.

orbitalselectiontest gains 4 real-async-path slots: asyncLoadBasisIsGuiAffine (asserts basis->thread() == GUI), plus ORCA/fchk/molden end-to-end no-wedge tests. Molden exercised; MOPAC aux deliberately skipped (no fixture).
tests: orbitalselectiontest 12/12 green; full ctest 44/44 under xvfb

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

Unresolved: GUI pixel render of a selected orbital not directly observed — the headless session could not automate the orbital-table click or view the framebuffer, so the manual-matrix render rows are recorded as pipeline-level (honest per design D4). Windows installer/MSVC leg not run locally: shared C++/Qt headers changed (comment-only OpenQube headers + extension test hooks), so the Windows CI job should confirm before merge.

Next: Trigger the Windows installer CI workflow (per AGENTS.md) to confirm MSVC builds; optionally archive the change via openspec-archive-change.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Orbital surfaces now render end-to-end for ORCA, Gaussian-fchk, and Molden files. The async basis parse was split so the OpenQube BasisSet subclass (and its internal QFutureWatcher) is constructed on the GUI thread and only filled on the worker — fixing the silent queue-wedge where a basis constructed on a QtConcurrent pool thread orphaned its watcher, so the cube `finished()` was never delivered and no orbital surface ever rendered.

Changed: parseBasisFile split into constructBasis (GUI thread: chooses the GaussianSet/SlaterSet subclass) + fillBasis (worker: the stack reader fills it). loadBasis constructs the basis before dispatch and the worker no longer deletes the GUI-affine basis (the GUI-thread continuation does, on both the stale-epoch and fill-failure paths). The D2 watcher-affinity invariant is documented at the async entry points. End-to-end regression tests drive the real async path.

Evidence: Full ctest suite 44/44 under `xvfb-run -a` (exit 0); `orbitalselectiontest` 12/12; the affinity assert fails (`Compared QObject pointers are not the same`) and the end-to-end test times out (~89s wedge at `Cube calculation started.`) when the fix is reverted to construct-on-worker (recorded red runs), then both green with the fix. Headless app run under xvfb + software GL advances past `Cube calculation started.` to `all calculations complete.` (10/10 orbitals).

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 → green. xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure → 44 passed, 0 failed. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/orbitalselectiontest → 12 passed, 0 failed.

durableSolution.reason: Task 3.1 requires running the instrumented-launch runbook on the affected machine (Debian 13 / Quadro FX 3800 / Mesa nouveau, a Core-profile-only GL stack). This machine is an AMD Vega that resolves a Compatibility profile, so it cannot reproduce the Core-profile-only scenario. The affected hardware is not accessible from this environment, so the field run is genuinely external-blocked.
durableSolution.durableFix: The guards in autoopttool.cpp are correct and the fix's behavior (no crash + graceful-bail diagnostic on enable() with no associated view) is verified by the automated test freshToolStartBeforePaintIsSafe (which emits the expected qWarning and asserts no session started) and forceFieldlessToolIsInert (paint early-return and mouseReleaseEvent null-worker skip). The only unverified piece is the confirmatory field run on the affected Core-profile machine.
durableSolution.evidence: Code inspection of autoopttool.cpp: enable() guards m_comboFF/m_glwidget and emits qWarning; paint() returns early when m_thread is null; mouseReleaseEvent() skips setPendingFixAtom when m_thread is null. Test autooptreprotest: freshToolStartBeforePaintIsSafe passes and logs 'AutoOptTool::enable: no view associated yet (m_glwidget null); touch the canvas first'; forceFieldlessToolIsInert passes. Local GL context resolves 'version 4 5 profile Compatibility' (llvmpipe), so the Core-profile-only affected stack is not reproducible here.
durableSolution.followUp: Run the instrumented-launch runbook on the affected machine (breakpoints on AutoOptTool::paint/enable logging m_glwidget, core dumps armed), activate AutoOpt and press Start without touching the canvas; confirm no crash and the graceful-bail qWarning, and record whether the overlay PAINT pass ever runs on that context (answers design.md's open question).

blocker.evidence: The affected machine (Debian 13 / Quadro FX 3800 / Mesa nouveau, Core-profile-only GL stack) is not accessible from this environment; the local machine is an AMD Vega resolving a Compatibility profile. The design.md D5 field-verification run requires that specific hardware.

durableDeferRecommendation.durableFix: The guards in autoopttool.cpp are correct and the fix's behavior (no crash + graceful-bail diagnostic on enable() with no associated view) is verified by the automated test freshToolStartBeforePaintIsSafe (which emits the expected qWarning and asserts no session started) and forceFieldlessToolIsInert (paint early-return and mouseReleaseEvent null-worker skip). The only unverified piece is the confirmatory field run on the affected Core-profile machine.
deferRecommendations: Task 3.1 requires running the instrumented-launch runbook on the affected machine (Debian 13 / Quadro FX 3800 / Mesa nouveau, a Core-profile-only GL stack). This machine is an AMD Vega that resolves a Compatibility profile, so it cannot reproduce the Core-profile-only scenario. The affected hardware is not accessible from this environment, so the field run is genuinely external-blocked.

durableSolution.durableFix: The guards in autoopttool.cpp are correct and the fix's behavior (no crash + graceful-bail diagnostic on enable() with no associated view) is verified by the automated test freshToolStartBeforePaintIsSafe (which emits the expected qWarning and asserts no session started) and forceFieldlessToolIsInert (paint early-return and mouseReleaseEvent null-worker skip). The only unverified piece is the confirmatory field run on the affected Core-profile machine.
durableSolution.evidence: Code inspection of autoopttool.cpp: enable() guards m_comboFF/m_glwidget and emits qWarning; paint() returns early when m_thread is null; mouseReleaseEvent() skips setPendingFixAtom when m_thread is null. Test autooptreprotest: freshToolStartBeforePaintIsSafe passes and logs 'AutoOptTool::enable: no view associated yet (m_glwidget null); touch the canvas first'; forceFieldlessToolIsInert passes. Local GL context resolves 'version 4 5 profile Compatibility' (llvmpipe), so the Core-profile-only affected stack is not reproducible here.
durableSolution.followUp: Run the instrumented-launch runbook on the affected machine (breakpoints on AutoOptTool::paint/enable logging m_glwidget, core dumps armed), activate AutoOpt and press Start without touching the canvas; confirm no crash and the graceful-bail qWarning, and record whether the overlay PAINT pass ever runs on that context (answers design.md's open question).

blocker.evidence: The affected machine (Debian 13 / Quadro FX 3800 / Mesa nouveau, Core-profile-only GL stack) is not accessible from this environment; the local machine is an AMD Vega resolving a Compatibility profile. The design.md D5 field-verification run requires that specific hardware.

Unresolved: The two live-GUI tests (liveDragAtomDuringAutoOpt, liveBondOrderClickDuringAutoOpt) skip on the offscreen platform; they pass under Xvfb elsewhere (per task 3.2 note). None otherwise.
Next: none.

Unresolved: The two live-GUI tests (liveDragAtomDuringAutoOpt, liveBondOrderClickDuringAutoOpt) skip on the offscreen platform; they pass under Xvfb elsewhere (per task 3.2 note). None otherwise.
Next: none.

Changed: AutoOptTool now null-guards m_glwidget (enable/disable/timerEvent) and m_thread (paint/mouseReleaseEvent), bailing gracefully with a qWarning diagnostic instead of dereferencing garbage pointers; behavior of a fully-initialized session is unchanged.
Evidence: gdb instrumented-launch runbook on the affected machine (Debian 13 / Quadro FX 3800 / Mesa 3.3 Core) confirmed m_glwidget=(nil) → "AutoOptTool::enable: no view associated yet (m_glwidget null); touch the canvas first" → m_running=0 → no crash (gdb exited only via timeout) and 0 PAINT-CALLED lines (overlay pass never fires on Core). Tests: autooptreprotest 19 passed / 0 failed / 2 skipped (live-GUI skip by design on offscreen); full ctest suite 46/46 passed, 0 failed.
Unresolved: The two live-GUI tests (liveDragAtomDuringAutoOpt, liveBondOrderClickDuringAutoOpt) skip on the offscreen platform; they pass under Xvfb elsewhere (per task 3.2 note). None otherwise.

Unresolved: The two live-GUI tests (liveDragAtomDuringAutoOpt, liveBondOrderClickDuringAutoOpt) skip on the offscreen platform; they pass under Xvfb elsewhere (per task 3.2 note). None otherwise.
Next: none.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The AutoOpt tool activation crash (uninitialized tool-lifetime pointers) is fixed and field-verified; the OpenSpec change "fix-autoopt-tool-activation-crash" is complete with all 10 tasks done.
Changed: AutoOptTool now null-guards m_glwidget (enable/disable/timerEvent) and m_thread (paint/mouseReleaseEvent), bailing gracefully with a qWarning diagnostic instead of dereferencing garbage pointers; behavior of a fully-initialized session is unchanged.
Evidence: gdb instrumented-launch runbook on the affected machine (Debian 13 / Quadro FX 3800 / Mesa 3.3 Core) confirmed m_glwidget=(nil) → "AutoOptTool::enable: no view associated yet (m_glwidget null); touch the canvas first" → m_running=0 → no crash (gdb exited only via timeout) and 0 PAINT-CALLED lines (overlay pass never fires on Core). Fix is on GitHub: origin/master = 373136000.
Tests: autooptreprotest 19 passed / 0 failed / 2 skipped (live-GUI skip by design on offscreen); full ctest suite 46/46 passed, 0 failed.
Unresolved: The two live-GUI tests (liveDragAtomDuringAutoOpt, liveBondOrderClickDuringAutoOpt) skip on the offscreen platform; they pass under Xvfb elsewhere (per task 3.2 note). None otherwise.
Next: none.

Unresolved: The two live-GUI tests (liveDragAtomDuringAutoOpt, liveBondOrderClickDuringAutoOpt) skip on the offscreen platform; they pass under Xvfb elsewhere (per task 3.2 note). None otherwise.
Next: none.

Unresolved: The two live-GUI tests (liveDragAtomDuringAutoOpt, liveBondOrderClickDuringAutoOpt) skip on the offscreen platform; they pass under Xvfb elsewhere (per task 3.2 note). None otherwise.
Next: none.

All verification-contract items have been independently checked. Final report:

## Audit report — fix-autoopt-tool-activation-crash (goal 20261104053905-3vq1vj)

**Changed paths confirmed carrying the work:**

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Uncolored orbital/VdW/density meshes now render on the modern tier — the change fixes the root cause where MeshGenerator produces vertices+normals with zero per-vertex colors and Mesh::valid() silently rejected them, dropping every orbital surface at SceneBuilder capture.
Changed: Mesh::valid() now accepts colors.size()==0 when vertex/normal counts agree (the ==1 and ==vertices.size() branches unchanged, so ESP-colored meshes are unaffected); SceneBuilder::drawMesh/drawColorMesh report a rejected mesh once instead of silently returning; new meshcapturetest pins the uncolored-mesh acceptance and the report-once diagnostic.
Evidence: Full Linux suite 45/45 under xvfb; Windows Installer run 41903246600 conclusion=success with both build-installer jobs green and 100% tests passed (meshcaptureTest 0.09s, autooptreproTest 25.40s); live ORCA repro confirmed 0→51,284 blue + 117,509 red isosurface pixels after an orbital click (pre-fix 0/0).
Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 (100%); xvfb-run ctest --test-dir build (100% tests passed, 0 failed out of 45); ctest -R meshcapture (pass); ctest -R mesh tests (meshcapture/meshrevision/meshstream/meshgenparallel/consumerparity all pass).
Unresolved: Reviewer noted a pre-existing, out-of-scope CartoonEngine bug (calls drawColorMesh with an uncolored mesh, causing per-frame qDebug on the modern tier; visual parity is maintained since it never rendered on the legacy tier either). Not a required task of this change.
Next: None required for this change; optionally follow up the CartoonEngine drawColorMesh-vs-drawMesh misuse as a separate change. — NOTE: low evidence density: no path:line evidence tokens and no verification gate rows — add file:line pointers (e.g. extensions/goal-recovery.ts:847) or a gateRows inventory so the terminal render is verifiable

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Uncolored orbital/VdW/density meshes now render on the modern tier — the change fixes the root cause where MeshGenerator produces vertices+normals with zero per-vertex colors and Mesh::valid() silently rejected them, dropping every orbital surface at SceneBuilder capture.
Changed: Mesh::valid() now accepts colors.size()==0 when vertex/normal counts agree (the ==1 and ==vertices.size() branches unchanged, so ESP-colored meshes are unaffected); SceneBuilder::drawMesh/drawColorMesh report a rejected mesh once instead of silently returning; new meshcapturetest pins the uncolored-mesh acceptance and the report-once diagnostic.
Evidence: Full Linux suite 45/45 under xvfb; Windows Installer run 41903246600 conclusion=success with both build-installer jobs green and 100% tests passed (meshcaptureTest 0.09s, autooptreproTest 25.40s); live ORCA repro confirmed 0→51,284 blue + 117,509 red isosurface pixels after an orbital click (pre-fix 0/0).
Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 (100%); xvfb-run ctest --test-dir build (100% tests passed, 0 failed out of 45); ctest -R meshcapture (pass); ctest -R mesh tests (meshcapture/meshrevision/meshstream/meshgenparallel/consumerparity all pass).
Unresolved: Reviewer noted a pre-existing, out-of-scope CartoonEngine bug (calls drawColorMesh with an uncolored mesh, causing per-frame qDebug on the modern tier; visual parity is maintained since it never rendered on the legacy tier either). Not a required task of this change.
Next: None required for this change; optionally follow up the CartoonEngine drawColorMesh-vs-drawMesh misuse as a separate change. — NOTE: low evidence density: no path:line evidence tokens and no verification gate rows — add file:line pointers (e.g. extensions/goal-recovery.ts:847) or a gateRows inventory so the terminal render is verifiable

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Uncolored orbital/VdW/density meshes now render on the modern tier — the change fixes the root cause where MeshGenerator produces vertices+normals with zero per-vertex colors and Mesh::valid() silently rejected them, dropping every orbital surface at SceneBuilder capture.
Changed: Mesh::valid() now accepts colors.size()==0 when vertex/normal counts agree (the ==1 and ==vertices.size() branches unchanged, so ESP-colored meshes are unaffected); SceneBuilder::drawMesh/drawColorMesh report a rejected mesh once instead of silently returning; new meshcapturetest pins the uncolored-mesh acceptance and the report-once diagnostic.
Evidence: Full Linux suite 45/45 under xvfb; Windows Installer run 41903246600 conclusion=success with both build-installer jobs green and 100% tests passed (meshcaptureTest 0.09s, autooptreproTest 25.40s); live ORCA repro confirmed 0→51,284 blue + 117,509 red isosurface pixels after an orbital click (pre-fix 0/0).
Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 (100%); xvfb-run ctest --test-dir build (100% tests passed, 0 failed out of 45); ctest -R meshcapture (pass); ctest -R mesh tests (meshcapture/meshrevision/meshstream/meshgenparallel/consumerparity all pass).
Unresolved: Reviewer noted a pre-existing, out-of-scope CartoonEngine bug (calls drawColorMesh with an uncolored mesh, causing per-frame qDebug on the modern tier; visual parity is maintained since it never rendered on the legacy tier either). Not a required task of this change.
Next: None required for this change; optionally follow up the CartoonEngine drawColorMesh-vs-drawMesh misuse as a separate change. — NOTE: low evidence density: no path:line evidence tokens and no verification gate rows — add file:line pointers (e.g. extensions/goal-recovery.ts:847) or a gateRows inventory so the terminal render is verifiable

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Uncolored orbital/VdW/density meshes now render on the modern tier — the change fixes the root cause where MeshGenerator produces vertices+normals with zero per-vertex colors and Mesh::valid() silently rejected them, dropping every orbital surface at SceneBuilder capture.
Changed: Mesh::valid() now accepts colors.size()==0 when vertex/normal counts agree (the ==1 and ==vertices.size() branches unchanged, so ESP-colored meshes are unaffected); SceneBuilder::drawMesh/drawColorMesh report a rejected mesh once instead of silently returning; new meshcapturetest pins the uncolored-mesh acceptance and the report-once diagnostic.
Evidence: Full Linux suite 45/45 under xvfb; Windows Installer run 41903246600 conclusion=success with both build-installer jobs green and 100% tests passed (meshcaptureTest 0.09s, autooptreproTest 25.40s); live ORCA repro confirmed 0→51,284 blue + 117,509 red isosurface pixels after an orbital click (pre-fix 0/0).
Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 (100%); xvfb-run ctest --test-dir build (100% tests passed, 0 failed out of 45); ctest -R meshcapture (pass); ctest -R mesh tests (meshcapture/meshrevision/meshstream/meshgenparallel/consumerparity all pass).
Unresolved: Reviewer noted a pre-existing, out-of-scope CartoonEngine bug (calls drawColorMesh with an uncolored mesh, causing per-frame qDebug on the modern tier; visual parity is maintained since it never rendered on the legacy tier either). Not a required task of this change.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Uncolored orbital/VdW/density meshes now render on the modern tier — the change fixes the root cause where MeshGenerator produces vertices+normals with zero per-vertex colors and Mesh::valid() silently rejected them, dropping every orbital surface at SceneBuilder capture.
Changed: Mesh::valid() now accepts colors.size()==0 when vertex/normal counts agree (the ==1 and ==vertices.size() branches unchanged, so ESP-colored meshes are unaffected); SceneBuilder::drawMesh/drawColorMesh report a rejected mesh once instead of silently returning; new meshcapturetest pins the uncolored-mesh acceptance and the report-once diagnostic.
Evidence: Full Linux suite 45/45 under xvfb; Windows Installer run 41903246600 conclusion=success with both build-installer jobs green and 100% tests passed (meshcaptureTest 0.09s, autooptreproTest 25.40s); live ORCA repro confirmed 0→51,284 blue + 117,509 red isosurface pixels after an orbital click (pre-fix 0/0).
Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 (100%); xvfb-run ctest --test-dir build (100% tests passed, 0 failed out of 45); ctest -R meshcapture (pass); ctest -R mesh tests (meshcapture/meshrevision/meshstream/meshgenparallel/consumerparity all pass).
Unresolved: Reviewer noted a pre-existing, out-of-scope CartoonEngine bug (calls drawColorMesh with an uncolored mesh, causing per-frame qDebug on the modern tier; visual parity is maintained since it never rendered on the legacy tier either). Not a required task of this change.
Next: None required for this change; optionally follow up the CartoonEngine drawColorMesh-vs-drawMesh misuse as a separate change. — NOTE: low evidence density: no path:line evidence tokens and no verification gate rows — add file:line pointers (e.g. extensions/goal-recovery.ts:847) or a gateRows inventory so the terminal render is verifiable
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
1. openspec instructions apply --change fix-orbital-mesh-render --json reports progress total=7 complete=7 remaining=0 (ids 1-7 all done: true).
2. D1: libavogadro/src/mesh.cpp:243-255 valid() accepts colors.size()==0 when vertices.size()==normals.size(); ==1 and ==vertices.size() branches preserved. D3: libavogadro/src/rendering/scenebuilder.cpp reportMeshInvalidOnce (static flag) called in drawMesh/drawColorMesh; matches repo "report once" convention. D4: libavogadro/tests/meshcapturetest.cpp (uncolored MeshGenerator cube valid+captured with instance color; corrupt 3v/2n mesh not captured, diagnostic fires exactly once). Spec scenarios: uncolored mesh renders with instance color; ESP per-vertex colors preserved (branches untouched); no silent loss (report-once); corrupt mesh reports once.
3. Commits 6576a9e47 and 623e0e2c3 on master (fast-forwarded from fix-orbital-mesh-render), pushed to origin (373136000..623e0e2c3). Working tree clean for change files.
4. Build: cmake --build build --parallel 8 -> [100%] Built target avogadro-app. Tests: xvfb-run ctest --test-dir build -> 100% tests passed, 0 failed out of 45. Windows: run 41903246600 conclusion=success; build-installer(tests) 50m31s + build-installer(installer) 47m47s both green; 100% tests passed 0 failed out of 45; meshcaptureTest Passed 0.09s; autooptreproTest Passed 25.40s. Mesh regression: ctest -R meshcapture|meshrevision|meshstream|meshgenparallel|consumerparity -> 5/5 pass.
5. Live repro (MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT under xvfb, Compatibility profile so GLPainter mesh flush runs): pre-fix bare geometry 0 blue/0 red pixels; post-fix after HOMO click 51,284 blue + 117,509 red pixels; LUMO click 490,714 red. No "fixed-function GLPainter skipped" message on the compat profile.
6. Artifacts (proposal/design/specs/tasks) match implementation; no substantive omission.
7. Repo coherent: change committed on master, push succeeded.
8. GLLA task mirror: ids 1-7 all status=complete; OPEN: none (active.jsonl parsed).
pendingCompletion.leftOut: The reviewer's P2 CartoonEngine finding (drawColorMesh with an uncolored mesh -> per-frame qDebug) is deliberately out of scope: it is a pre-existing bug in a different engine, and this change's non-goals explicitly exclude engines other than SurfaceEngine; visual parity is already maintained. No fix applied for it.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Uncolored orbital/VdW/density meshes now render on the modern tier — the change fixes the root cause where MeshGenerator produces vertices+normals with zero per-vertex colors and Mesh::valid() silently rejected them, dropping every orbital surface at SceneBuilder capture.
Changed: Mesh::valid() now accepts colors.size()==0 when vertex/normal counts agree (the ==1 and ==vertices.size() branches unchanged, so ESP-colored meshes are unaffected); SceneBuilder::drawMesh/drawColorMesh report a rejected mesh once instead of silently returning; new meshcapturetest pins the uncolored-mesh acceptance and the report-once diagnostic.
Evidence: Full Linux suite 45/45 under xvfb; Windows Installer run 41903246600 conclusion=success with both build-installer jobs green and 100% tests passed (meshcaptureTest 0.09s, autooptreproTest 25.40s); live ORCA repro confirmed 0→51,284 blue + 117,509 red isosurface pixels after an orbital click (pre-fix 0/0).
Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 (100%); xvfb-run ctest --test-dir build (100% tests passed, 0 failed out of 45); ctest -R meshcapture (pass); ctest -R mesh tests (meshcapture/meshrevision/meshstream/meshgenparallel/consumerparity all pass).
Unresolved: Reviewer noted a pre-existing, out-of-scope CartoonEngine bug (calls drawColorMesh with an uncolored mesh, causing per-frame qDebug on the modern tier; visual parity is maintained since it never rendered on the legacy tier either). Not a required task of this change.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Uncolored orbital/VdW/density meshes now render on the modern tier — the change fixes the root cause where MeshGenerator produces vertices+normals with zero per-vertex colors and Mesh::valid() silently rejected them, dropping every orbital surface at SceneBuilder capture.
Changed: Mesh::valid() now accepts colors.size()==0 when vertex/normal counts agree (the ==1 and ==vertices.size() branches unchanged, so ESP-colored meshes are unaffected); SceneBuilder::drawMesh/drawColorMesh report a rejected mesh once instead of silently returning; new meshcapturetest pins the uncolored-mesh acceptance and the report-once diagnostic.
Evidence: Full Linux suite 45/45 under xvfb; Windows Installer run 41903246600 conclusion=success with both build-installer jobs green and 100% tests passed (meshcaptureTest 0.09s, autooptreproTest 25.40s); live ORCA repro confirmed 0→51,284 blue + 117,509 red isosurface pixels after an orbital click (pre-fix 0/0).
Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 (100%); xvfb-run ctest --test-dir build (100% tests passed, 0 failed out of 45); ctest -R meshcapture (pass); ctest -R mesh tests (meshcapture/meshrevision/meshstream/meshgenparallel/consumerparity all pass).
Unresolved: Reviewer noted a pre-existing, out-of-scope CartoonEngine bug (calls drawColorMesh with an uncolored mesh, causing per-frame qDebug on the modern tier; visual parity is maintained since it never rendered on the legacy tier either). Not a required task of this change.

Unresolved: Reviewer noted a pre-existing, out-of-scope CartoonEngine bug (calls drawColorMesh with an uncolored mesh, causing per-frame qDebug on the modern tier; visual parity is maintained since it never rendered on the legacy tier either). Not a required task of this change.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Uncolored orbital/VdW/density meshes now render on the modern tier — the change fixes the root cause where MeshGenerator produces vertices+normals with zero per-vertex colors and Mesh::valid() silently rejected them, dropping every orbital surface at SceneBuilder capture.
Changed: Mesh::valid() now accepts colors.size()==0 when vertex/normal counts agree (the ==1 and ==vertices.size() branches unchanged, so ESP-colored meshes are unaffected); SceneBuilder::drawMesh/drawColorMesh report a rejected mesh once instead of silently returning; new meshcapturetest pins the uncolored-mesh acceptance and the report-once diagnostic.
Evidence: Full Linux suite 45/45 under xvfb; Windows Installer run 41903246600 conclusion=success with both build-installer jobs green and 100% tests passed (meshcaptureTest 0.09s, autooptreproTest 25.40s); live ORCA repro confirmed 0→51,284 blue + 117,509 red isosurface pixels after an orbital click (pre-fix 0/0).
Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 (100%); xvfb-run ctest --test-dir build (100% tests passed, 0 failed out of 45); ctest -R meshcapture (pass); ctest -R mesh tests (meshcapture/meshrevision/meshstream/meshgenparallel/consumerparity all pass).
Unresolved: Reviewer noted a pre-existing, out-of-scope CartoonEngine bug (calls drawColorMesh with an uncolored mesh, causing per-frame qDebug on the modern tier; visual parity is maintained since it never rendered on the legacy tier either). Not a required task of this change.
Next: None required for this change; optionally follow up the CartoonEngine drawColorMesh-vs-drawMesh misuse as a separate change. — NOTE: low evidence density: no path:line evidence tokens and no verification gate rows — add file:line pointers (e.g. extensions/goal-recovery.ts:847) or a gateRows inventory so the terminal render is verifiable
