pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Uncolored orbital/VdW/density meshes now render on the modern tier — the change fixes the root cause where MeshGenerator produces vertices+normals with zero per-vertex colors and Mesh::valid() silently rejected them, dropping every orbital surface at SceneBuilder capture.
Changed: Mesh::valid() now accepts colors.size()==0 when vertex/normal counts agree (the ==1 and ==vertices.size() branches unchanged, so ESP-colored meshes are unaffected); SceneBuilder::drawMesh/drawColorMesh report a rejected mesh once instead of silently returning; new meshcapturetest pins the uncolored-mesh acceptance and the report-once diagnostic.
Evidence: Full Linux suite 45/45 under xvfb; Windows Installer run 41903246600 conclusion=success with both build-installer jobs green and 100% tests passed (meshcaptureTest 0.09s, autooptreproTest 25.40s); live ORCA repro confirmed 0→51,284 blue + 117,509 red isosurface pixels after an orbital click (pre-fix 0/0).
Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 (100%); xvfb-run ctest --test-dir build (100% tests passed, 0 failed out of 45); ctest -R meshcapture (pass); ctest -R mesh tests (meshcapture/meshrevision/meshstream/meshgenparallel/consumerparity all pass).
Unresolved: Reviewer noted a pre-existing, out-of-scope CartoonEngine bug (calls drawColorMesh with an uncolored mesh, causing per-frame qDebug on the modern tier; visual parity is maintained since it never rendered on the legacy tier either). Not a required task of this change.
Next: None required for this change; optionally follow up the CartoonEngine drawColorMesh-vs-drawMesh misuse as a separate change. — NOTE: low evidence density: no path:line evidence tokens and no verification gate rows — add file:line pointers (e.g. extensions/goal-recovery.ts:847) or a gateRows inventory so the terminal render is verifiable

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Uncolored orbital/VdW/density meshes now render on the modern tier — the change fixes the root cause where MeshGenerator produces vertices+normals with zero per-vertex colors and Mesh::valid() silently rejected them, dropping every orbital surface at SceneBuilder capture.
Changed: Mesh::valid() now accepts colors.size()==0 when vertex/normal counts agree (the ==1 and ==vertices.size() branches unchanged, so ESP-colored meshes are unaffected); SceneBuilder::drawMesh/drawColorMesh report a rejected mesh once instead of silently returning; new meshcapturetest pins the uncolored-mesh acceptance and the report-once diagnostic.
Evidence: Full Linux suite 45/45 under xvfb; Windows Installer run 41903246600 conclusion=success with both build-installer jobs green and 100% tests passed (meshcaptureTest 0.09s, autooptreproTest 25.40s); live ORCA repro confirmed 0→51,284 blue + 117,509 red isosurface pixels after an orbital click (pre-fix 0/0).
Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 (100%); xvfb-run ctest --test-dir build (100% tests passed, 0 failed out of 45); ctest -R meshcapture (pass); ctest -R mesh tests (meshcapture/meshrevision/meshstream/meshgenparallel/consumerparity all pass).
Unresolved: Reviewer noted a pre-existing, out-of-scope CartoonEngine bug (calls drawColorMesh with an uncolored mesh, causing per-frame qDebug on the modern tier; visual parity is maintained since it never rendered on the legacy tier either). Not a required task of this change.
Next: None required for this change; optionally follow up the CartoonEngine drawColorMesh-vs-drawMesh misuse as a separate change. — NOTE: low evidence density: no path:line evidence tokens and no verification gate rows — add file:line pointers (e.g. extensions/goal-recovery.ts:847) or a gateRows inventory so the terminal render is verifiable

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Uncolored orbital/VdW/density meshes now render on the modern tier — the change fixes the root cause where MeshGenerator produces vertices+normals with zero per-vertex colors and Mesh::valid() silently rejected them, dropping every orbital surface at SceneBuilder capture.

Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 (100%); xvfb-run ctest --test-dir build (100% tests passed, 0 failed out of 45); ctest -R meshcapture (pass); ctest -R mesh tests (meshcapture/meshrevision/meshstream/meshgenparallel/consumerparity all pass).

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: Uncolored orbital/VdW/density meshes now render on the modern tier — the change fixes the root cause where MeshGenerator produces vertices+normals with zero per-vertex colors and Mesh::valid() silently rejected them, dropping every orbital surface at SceneBuilder capture.

Evidence: Full Linux suite 45/45 under xvfb; Windows Installer run 41903246600 conclusion=success with both build-installer jobs green and 100% tests passed (meshcaptureTest 0.09s, autooptreproTest 25.40s); live ORCA repro confirmed 0→51,284 blue + 117,509 red isosurface pixels after an orbital click (pre-fix 0/0).
Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 (100%); xvfb-run ctest --test-dir build (100% tests passed, 0 failed out of 45); ctest -R meshcapture (pass); ctest -R mesh tests (meshcapture/meshrevision/meshstream/meshgenparallel/consumerparity all pass).
Unresolved: Reviewer noted a pre-existing, out-of-scope CartoonEngine bug (calls drawColorMesh with an uncolored mesh, causing per-frame qDebug on the modern tier; visual parity is maintained since it never rendered on the legacy tier either). Not a required task of this change.

Outcome: Uncolored orbital/VdW/density meshes now render on the modern tier — the change fixes the root cause where MeshGenerator produces vertices+normals with zero per-vertex colors and Mesh::valid() silently rejected them, dropping every orbital surface at SceneBuilder capture.

Evidence: Full Linux suite 45/45 under xvfb; Windows Installer run 41903246600 conclusion=success with both build-installer jobs green and 100% tests passed (meshcaptureTest 0.09s, autooptreproTest 25.40s); live ORCA repro confirmed 0→51,284 blue + 117,509 red isosurface pixels after an orbital click (pre-fix 0/0).

Unresolved: Reviewer noted a pre-existing, out-of-scope CartoonEngine bug (calls drawColorMesh with an uncolored mesh, causing per-frame qDebug on the modern tier; visual parity is maintained since it never rendered on the legacy tier either). Not a required task of this change.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: Uncolored orbital/VdW/density meshes now render on the modern tier — the change fixes the root cause where MeshGenerator produces vertices+normals with zero per-vertex colors and Mesh::valid() silently rejected them, dropping every orbital surface at SceneBuilder capture.
Changed: Mesh::valid() now accepts colors.size()==0 when vertex/normal counts agree (the ==1 and ==vertices.size() branches unchanged, so ESP-colored meshes are unaffected); SceneBuilder::drawMesh/drawColorMesh report a rejected mesh once instead of silently returning; new meshcapturetest pins the uncolored-mesh acceptance and the report-once diagnostic.
Evidence: Full Linux suite 45/45 under xvfb; Windows Installer run 41903246600 conclusion=success with both build-installer jobs green and 100% tests passed (meshcaptureTest 0.09s, autooptreproTest 25.40s); live ORCA repro confirmed 0→51,284 blue + 117,509 red isosurface pixels after an orbital click (pre-fix 0/0).
Tests: cmake --build build --parallel 8 (100%); xvfb-run ctest --test-dir build (100% tests passed, 0 failed out of 45); ctest -R meshcapture (pass); ctest -R mesh tests (meshcapture/meshrevision/meshstream/meshgenparallel/consumerparity all pass).
Unresolved: Reviewer noted a pre-existing, out-of-scope CartoonEngine bug (calls drawColorMesh with an uncolored mesh, causing per-frame qDebug on the modern tier; visual parity is maintained since it never rendered on the legacy tier either). Not a required task of this change.
Next: None required for this change; optionally follow up the CartoonEngine drawColorMesh-vs-drawMesh misuse as a separate change. — NOTE: low evidence density: no path:line evidence tokens and no verification gate rows — add file:line pointers (e.g. extensions/goal-recovery.ts:847) or a gateRows inventory so the terminal render is verifiable

# Audit Report — fix-orbital-mesh-render

**Scope**: 5 changed files + verification contract. All claims cross-checked against the live tree, freshly executed tests, GitHub Actions API, and fresh screenshots inspected with native vision.

## Findings

**Implementation present and correct.**
- `libavogadro/src/mesh.cpp:243-255` — `valid()` now accepts `m_colors.size() == 0` when vertex/normal counts agree; the `==1` and `==vertices.size()` branches are byte-for-byte preserved (verified via `git show 6576a9e47 -- libavogadro/src/mesh.cpp`: `-if (m_colors.size() == 1 || ...)` → `+if (m_colors.size() == 0 || m_colors.size() == 1 || ...)`).
- `libavogadro/src/rendering/scenebuilder.cpp:58-67` — `reportMeshInvalidOnce` shared static flag, called at scenebuilder.cpp:174 (drawMesh) and :192 (drawColorMesh) on the `!mesh.valid()` path.
- `libavogadro/tests/meshcapturetest.cpp` — real headless test: uncolored `MeshGenerator` product asserted valid, captured via both emitters with instance color; 3v/2n corrupt mesh asserted not captured with diagnostic tally == 1 (exactly-once). Registered in `libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt:143-151` with a correct MSVC dllexport rationale.

**Independently executed verification (not taken from claims):**
- Full suite run by me: `xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build` → **`100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 45`**.
- Mesh regressions: `meshcapture|meshrevision|meshstream|meshgenparallel|consumerparity` → 5/5 pass.
- Windows CI via `gh run view 41903246600 --repo thosoo/avogadro`: `conclusion: success`, both `build-installer` jobs success, `headSha: 6576a9e47...` — the run executed the code commit; local HEAD `623e0e2c3` differs only by tasks.md evidence text.
- Visual repro (fresh images, native inspection): `/tmp/orbrepro/shot_pre.png` (21:00) shows the bare CH₄-like molecule with **no isosurface**; `/tmp/orbrepro/shot_homo2.png` (21:04) shows large **red + blue two-lobed orbital isosurface** surrounding the molecule with the HOMO row highlighted in the orbital panel. This matches the spec scenario "ORCA orbital surfaces are visible" (positive and negative lobes rendering). Critique verbatim: *pre-fix frame shows only ball-and-stick geometry on black canvas; post-fix HOMO frame shows a translucent red lobe over the carbon/hydrogen region and a blue lobe below — the expected p-type HOMO pair — plus a selected HOMO row (-10.569 eV); rendering quality consistent with the legacy tier; no stale/partial geometry visible.*

**Advisory (non-blocking, per change scope):**
- Reviewer's CartoonEngine `drawColorMesh` note (`libavogadro/src/engines/cartoonengine.cpp:166`) — pre-existing caller outside the changed paths, explicitly assessed in tasks.md 4.4 evidence; log-noise only, no visual regression.
- Working-tree noise (tracked `build-asan/` deletions, `.pi-glla/` churn) predates/outside the change; source paths for the change are clean and `master == origin/master == 623e0e2c3`.

No defect found in the changed paths; every contract item verified with primary evidence.

**Scope**: 5 changed files + verification contract. All claims cross-checked against the live tree, freshly executed tests, GitHub Actions API, and fresh screenshots inspected with native vision.

## Findings

**Implementation present and correct.**
- `libavogadro/src/mesh.cpp:243-255` — `valid()` now accepts `m_colors.size() == 0` when vertex/normal counts agree; the `==1` and `==vertices.size()` branches are byte-for-byte preserved (verified via `git show 6576a9e47 -- libavogadro/src/mesh.cpp`: `-if (m_colors.size() == 1 || ...)` → `+if (m_colors.size() == 0 || m_colors.size() == 1 || ...)`).
- `libavogadro/src/rendering/scenebuilder.cpp:58-67` — `reportMeshInvalidOnce` shared static flag, called at scenebuilder.cpp:174 (drawMesh) and :192 (drawColorMesh) on the `!mesh.valid()` path.
- `libavogadro/tests/meshcapturetest.cpp` — real headless test: uncolored `MeshGenerator` product asserted valid, captured via both emitters with instance color; 3v/2n corrupt mesh asserted not captured with diagnostic tally == 1 (exactly-once). Registered in `libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt:143-151` with a correct MSVC dllexport rationale.

**Independently executed verification (not taken from claims):**
- Full suite run by me: `xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build` → **`100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 45`**.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The DrawTool click-to-extend gesture (ChemDraw-style) is implemented, verified, and CI-green on both Linux (Qt6) and Windows (MSVC installer). Changed: clicking an atom of the currently-selected element now grows the molecule — a new atom of that element is placed at a chemically plausible, deterministic position (sp 180°, sp2 120°, sp3 ~109.47°; an allene-center Sp atom, whose two double-bonded neighbors are collinear, falls back to perpendicular to the multiple-bond axis) at the covalent-radii-sum bond length, bonded with the selected order, and committed as one undoable step with the full adjust-hydrogens choreography; different-element clicks keep the existing alchemy; three pre-existing stroke-state bugs (unguarded m_forceField derefs, early-return cleanup skips, lock-failure stale state) are fixed; the tooltip documents click/drag/right-click. Evidence: OpenSpec state=all_done (16/16 tasks); full suite 46/46 under Xvfb; placementtest 15/15; autooptreprotest 24/24 including three new live click-extend scenarios; Qt6 CI run 41993280536 success; Windows Installer run 41993280463 success. Tests: cmake --build build && ctest 46/46 pass; placementtest 15/15 pass; live autooptreprotest under Xvfb 24/24 pass. Unresolved: a pre-existing ChangeElementDrawCommand element-0 path on a jittered same-element click (reviewer finding 4) is rejected as out of scope — byte-identical to pre-change behavior, and a naive "fix" would regress the dummy-atom (element 0) alchemy case; the live GUI tests QSKIP under the offscreen ctest platform and run under Xvfb. Next: archive the change (openspec archive) when ready. — NOTE: low evidence density: no path:line evidence tokens and no verification gate rows — add file:line pointers (e.g. extensions/goal-recovery.ts:847) or a gateRows inventory so the terminal render is verifiable

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The DrawTool click-to-extend gesture (ChemDraw-style) is implemented, verified, and CI-green on both Linux (Qt6) and Windows (MSVC installer). Changed: clicking an atom of the currently-selected element now grows the molecule — a new atom of that element is placed at a chemically plausible, deterministic position (sp 180°, sp2 120°, sp3 ~109.47°; an allene-center Sp atom, whose two double-bonded neighbors are collinear, falls back to perpendicular to the multiple-bond axis) at the covalent-radii-sum bond length, bonded with the selected order, and committed as one undoable step with the full adjust-hydrogens choreography; different-element clicks keep the existing alchemy; three pre-existing stroke-state bugs (unguarded m_forceField derefs, early-return cleanup skips, lock-failure stale state) are fixed; the tooltip documents click/drag/right-click. Evidence: OpenSpec state=all_done (16/16 tasks); full suite 46/46 under Xvfb; placementtest 15/15; autooptreprotest 24/24 including three new live click-extend scenarios; Qt6 CI run 41993280536 success; Windows Installer run 41993280463 success. Tests: cmake --build build && ctest 46/46 pass; placementtest 15/15 pass; live autooptreprotest under Xvfb 24/24 pass. Unresolved: a pre-existing ChangeElementDrawCommand element-0 path on a jittered same-element click (reviewer finding 4) is rejected as out of scope — byte-identical to pre-change behavior, and a naive "fix" would regress the dummy-atom (element 0) alchemy case; the live GUI tests QSKIP under the offscreen ctest platform and run under Xvfb. Next: archive the change (openspec archive) when ready. — NOTE: low evidence density: no path:line evidence tokens and no verification gate rows — add file:line pointers (e.g. extensions/goal-recovery.ts:847) or a gateRows inventory so the terminal render is verifiable

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The DrawTool click-to-extend gesture (ChemDraw-style) is implemented, verified, and CI-green on both Linux (Qt6) and Windows (MSVC installer). Changed: clicking an atom of the currently-selected element now grows the molecule — a new atom of that element is placed at a chemically plausible, deterministic position (sp 180°, sp2 120°, sp3 ~109.47°; an allene-center Sp atom, whose two double-bonded neighbors are collinear, falls back to perpendicular to the multiple-bond axis) at the covalent-radii-sum bond length, bonded with the selected order, and committed as one undoable step with the full adjust-hydrogens choreography; different-element clicks keep the existing alchemy; three pre-existing stroke-state bugs (unguarded m_forceField derefs, early-return cleanup skips, lock-failure stale state) are fixed; the tooltip documents click/drag/right-click. Evidence: OpenSpec state=all_done (16/16 tasks); full suite 46/46 under Xvfb; placementtest 15/15; autooptreprotest 24/24 including three new live click-extend scenarios; Qt6 CI run 41993280536 success; Windows Installer run 41993280463 success. Tests: cmake --build build && ctest 46/46 pass; placementtest 15/15 pass; live autooptreprotest under Xvfb 24/24 pass. Unresolved: a pre-existing ChangeElementDrawCommand element-0 path on a jittered same-element click (reviewer finding 4) is rejected as out of scope — byte-identical to pre-change behavior, and a naive "fix" would regress the dummy-atom (element 0) alchemy case; the live GUI tests QSKIP under the offscreen ctest platform and run under Xvfb. pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The DrawTool click-to-extend gesture (ChemDraw-style) is implemented, verified, and CI-green on both Linux (Qt6) and Windows (MSVC installer). Changed: clicking an atom of the currently-selected element now grows the molecule — a new atom of that element is placed at a chemically plausible, deterministic position (sp 180°, sp2 120°, sp3 ~109.47°; an allene-center Sp atom, whose two double-bonded neighbors are collinear, falls back to perpendicular to the multiple-bond axis) at the covalent-radii-sum bond length, bonded with the selected order, and committed as one undoable step with the full adjust-hydrogens choreography; different-element clicks keep the existing alchemy; three pre-existing stroke-state bugs (unguarded m_forceField derefs, early-return cleanup skips, lock-failure stale state) are fixed; the tooltip documents click/drag/right-click. Evidence: OpenSpec state=all_done (16/16 tasks); full suite 46/46 under Xvfb; placementtest 15/15; autooptreprotest 24/24 including three new live click-extend scenarios; Qt6 CI run 41993280536 success; Windows Installer run 41993280463 success. Tests: cmake --build build && ctest 46/46 pass; placementtest 15/15 pass; live autooptreprotest under Xvfb 24/24 pass. Unresolved: a pre-existing ChangeElementDrawCommand element-0 path on a jittered same-element click (reviewer finding 4) is rejected as out of scope — byte-identical to pre-change behavior, and a naive "fix" would regress the dummy-atom (element 0) alchemy case; the live GUI tests QSKIP under the offscreen ctest platform and run under Xvfb. Next: archive the change (openspec archive) when ready. — NOTE: low evidence density: no path:line evidence tokens and no verification gate rows — add file:line pointers (e.g. extensions/goal-recovery.ts:847) or a gateRows inventory so the terminal render is verifiable
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:

1. OpenSpec state: `openspec instructions apply --change add-draw-tool-click-extend --json` returns state="all_done", isComplete=true, and all 16 tasks (id 1-16) report done=true.
2. GLLA mirror: `.pi-glla/goals/20261105050850-00so7o.md` task list shows all 16 tasks marked "- [x]" (0 open); the continuation reports 16/16 done, no pending task.
3. Build: `cmake --build build --parallel -j8` exit 0.
4. Full suite: `xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure -j8` -> 46/46 passed (100%).
5. Placement unit test: `./build/bin/placementtest` (offscreen) -> 15/15 passed.
6. Live gesture: `xvfb-run -a ./build/bin/autooptreprotest` (real xcb GL context) -> 24/24 passed, including the three new click-extend scenarios.
7. Qt6 CI on HEAD 87cbfe04f: run 41993280536 completed success (5/5 jobs).
8. Windows Installer CI on HEAD 87cbfe04f: run 41993280463 completed success (2/2 jobs).
9. Repository coherent: HEAD=87cbfe04f in sync with upstream; all source/OpenSpec changes committed and pushed.

Reviewer findings (5.4) disposition: Finding 1 (MAJOR, allene-center spec conformance) ACCEPT — perpendicular fallback + spec amendment + scenario/tests. Finding 2 (MINOR, design.md D2 signs) ACCEPT. Finding 3 (MINOR, missing n==2 Sp2/Sp tests) ACCEPT. Finding 4 (MINOR, pre-existing element-0 path) REJECT — out of scope, byte-identical to pre-change. Finding 5 (NIT, redundant clickBegin) ACCEPT-as-harmless. Finding 6 (NIT, lock-failure not clearing m_clickExtendCandidate) ACCEPT.

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The DrawTool click-to-extend gesture (ChemDraw-style) is implemented, verified, and CI-green on both Linux (Qt6) and Windows (MSVC installer). Changed: clicking an atom of the currently-selected element now grows the molecule — a new atom of that element is placed at a chemically plausible, deterministic position (sp 180°, sp2 120°, sp3 ~109.47°; an allene-center Sp atom, whose two double-bonded neighbors are collinear, falls back to perpendicular to the multiple-bond axis) at the covalent-radii-sum bond length, bonded with the selected order, and committed as one undoable step with the full adjust-hydrogens choreography; different-element clicks keep the existing alchemy; three pre-existing stroke-state bugs (unguarded m_forceField derefs, early-return cleanup skips, lock-failure stale state) are fixed; the tooltip documents click/drag/right-click. Evidence: OpenSpec state=all_done (16/16 tasks); full suite 46/46 under Xvfb; placementtest 15/15; autooptreprotest 24/24 including three new live click-extend scenarios; Qt6 CI run 41993280536 success; Windows Installer run 41993280463 success. completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The DrawTool click-to-extend gesture (ChemDraw-style) is implemented, verified, and CI-green on both Linux (Qt6) and Windows (MSVC installer). Changed: clicking an atom of the currently-selected element now grows the molecule — a new atom of that element is placed at a chemically plausible, deterministic position (sp 180°, sp2 120°, sp3 ~109.47°; an allene-center Sp atom, whose two double-bonded neighbors are collinear, falls back to perpendicular to the multiple-bond axis) at the covalent-radii-sum bond length, bonded with the selected order, and committed as one undoable step with the full adjust-hydrogens choreography; different-element clicks keep the existing alchemy; three pre-existing stroke-state bugs (unguarded m_forceField derefs, early-return cleanup skips, lock-failure stale state) are fixed; the tooltip documents click/drag/right-click. Evidence: OpenSpec state=all_done (16/16 tasks); full suite 46/46 under Xvfb; placementtest 15/15; autooptreprotest 24/24 including three new live click-extend scenarios; Qt6 CI run 41993280536 success; Windows Installer run 41993280463 success. Tests: cmake --build build && ctest 46/46 pass; placementtest 15/15 pass; live autooptreprotest under Xvfb 24/24 pass. Unresolved: a pre-existing ChangeElementDrawCommand element-0 path on a jittered same-element click (reviewer finding 4) is rejected as out of scope — byte-identical to pre-change behavior, and a naive "fix" would regress the dummy-atom (element 0) alchemy case; the live GUI tests QSKIP under the offscreen ctest platform and run under Xvfb. Next: archive the change (openspec archive) when ready. — NOTE: low evidence density: no path:line evidence tokens and no verification gate rows — add file:line pointers (e.g. extensions/goal-recovery.ts:847) or a gateRows inventory so the terminal render is verifiable

Changed: clicking an atom of the currently-selected element now grows the molecule — a new atom of that element is placed at a chemically plausible, deterministic position (sp 180°, sp2 120°, sp3 ~109.47°; an allene-center Sp atom, whose two double-bonded neighbors are collinear, falls back to perpendicular to the multiple-bond axis) at the covalent-radii-sum bond length, bonded with the selected order, and committed as one undoable step with the full adjust-hydrogens choreography; different-element clicks keep the existing alchemy; three pre-existing stroke-state bugs (unguarded m_forceField derefs, early-return cleanup skips, lock-failure stale state) are fixed; the tooltip documents click/drag/right-click. Evidence: OpenSpec state=all_done (16/16 tasks); full suite 46/46 under Xvfb; placementtest 15/15; autooptreprotest 24/24 including three new live click-extend scenarios; Qt6 CI run 41993280536 success; Windows Installer run 41993280463 success. Tests: cmake --build build && ctest 46/46 pass; placementtest 15/15 pass; live autooptreprotest under Xvfb 24/24 pass. Unresolved: a pre-existing ChangeElementDrawCommand element-0 path on a jittered same-element click (reviewer finding 4) is rejected as out of scope — byte-identical to pre-change behavior, and a naive "fix" would regress the dummy-atom (element 0) alchemy case; the live GUI tests QSKIP under the offscreen ctest platform and run under Xvfb. pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The DrawTool click-to-extend gesture (ChemDraw-style) is implemented, verified, and CI-green on both Linux (Qt6) and Windows (MSVC installer). Changed: clicking an atom of the currently-selected element now grows the molecule — a new atom of that element is placed at a chemically plausible, deterministic position (sp 180°, sp2 120°, sp3 ~109.47°; an allene-center Sp atom, whose two double-bonded neighbors are collinear, falls back to perpendicular to the multiple-bond axis) at the covalent-radii-sum bond length, bonded with the selected order, and committed as one undoable step with the full adjust-hydrogens choreography; different-element clicks keep the existing alchemy; three pre-existing stroke-state bugs (unguarded m_forceField derefs, early-return cleanup skips, lock-failure stale state) are fixed; the tooltip documents click/drag/right-click. Evidence: OpenSpec state=all_done (16/16 tasks); full suite 46/46 under Xvfb; placementtest 15/15; autooptreprotest 24/24 including three new live click-extend scenarios; Qt6 CI run 41993280536 success; Windows Installer run 41993280463 success. Tests: cmake --build build && ctest 46/46 pass; placementtest 15/15 pass; live autooptreprotest under Xvfb 24/24 pass. Unresolved: a pre-existing ChangeElementDrawCommand element-0 path on a jittered same-element click (reviewer finding 4) is rejected as out of scope — byte-identical to pre-change behavior, and a naive "fix" would regress the dummy-atom (element 0) alchemy case; the live GUI tests QSKIP under the offscreen ctest platform and run under Xvfb. pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The DrawTool click-to-extend gesture (ChemDraw-style) is implemented, verified, and CI-green on both Linux (Qt6) and Windows (MSVC installer). Changed: clicking an atom of the currently-selected element now grows the molecule — a new atom of that element is placed at a chemically plausible, deterministic position (sp 180°, sp2 120°, sp3 ~109.47°; an allene-center Sp atom, whose two double-bonded neighbors are collinear, falls back to perpendicular to the multiple-bond axis) at the covalent-radii-sum bond length, bonded with the selected order, and committed as one undoable step with the full adjust-hydrogens choreography; different-element clicks keep the existing alchemy; three pre-existing stroke-state bugs (unguarded m_forceField derefs, early-return cleanup skips, lock-failure stale state) are fixed; the tooltip documents click/drag/right-click. Evidence: OpenSpec state=all_done (16/16 tasks); full suite 46/46 under Xvfb; placementtest 15/15; autooptreprotest 24/24 including three new live click-extend scenarios; Qt6 CI run 41993280536 success; Windows Installer run 41993280463 success. Tests: cmake --build build && ctest 46/46 pass; placementtest 15/15 pass; live autooptreprotest under Xvfb 24/24 pass. Unresolved: a pre-existing ChangeElementDrawCommand element-0 path on a jittered same-element click (reviewer finding 4) is rejected as out of scope — byte-identical to pre-change behavior, and a naive "fix" would regress the dummy-atom (element 0) alchemy case; the live GUI tests QSKIP under the offscreen ctest platform and run under Xvfb. Next: archive the change (openspec archive) when ready. — NOTE: low evidence density: no path:line evidence tokens and no verification gate rows — add file:line pointers (e.g. extensions/goal-recovery.ts:847) or a gateRows inventory so the terminal render is verifiable

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The DrawTool click-to-extend gesture (ChemDraw-style) is implemented, verified, and CI-green on both Linux (Qt6) and Windows (MSVC installer). Changed: clicking an atom of the currently-selected element now grows the molecule — a new atom of that element is placed at a chemically plausible, deterministic position (sp 180°, sp2 120°, sp3 ~109.47°; an allene-center Sp atom, whose two double-bonded neighbors are collinear, falls back to perpendicular to the multiple-bond axis) at the covalent-radii-sum bond length, bonded with the selected order, and committed as one undoable step with the full adjust-hydrogens choreography; different-element clicks keep the existing alchemy; three pre-existing stroke-state bugs (unguarded m_forceField derefs, early-return cleanup skips, lock-failure stale state) are fixed; the tooltip documents click/drag/right-click. Evidence: OpenSpec state=all_done (16/16 tasks); full suite 46/46 under Xvfb; placementtest 15/15; autooptreprotest 24/24 including three new live click-extend scenarios; Qt6 CI run 41993280536 success; Windows Installer run 41993280463 success. Tests: cmake --build build && ctest 46/46 pass; placementtest 15/15 pass; live autooptreprotest under Xvfb 24/24 pass. Unresolved: a pre-existing ChangeElementDrawCommand element-0 path on a jittered same-element click (reviewer finding 4) is rejected as out of scope — byte-identical to pre-change behavior, and a naive "fix" would regress the dummy-atom (element 0) alchemy case; the live GUI tests QSKIP under the offscreen ctest platform and run under Xvfb. Next: archive the change (openspec archive) when ready. — NOTE: low evidence density: no path:line evidence tokens and no verification gate rows — add file:line pointers (e.g. extensions/goal-recovery.ts:847) or a gateRows inventory so the terminal render is verifiable

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The DrawTool click-to-extend gesture (ChemDraw-style) is implemented, verified, and CI-green on both Linux (Qt6) and Windows (MSVC installer). Changed: clicking an atom of the currently-selected element now grows the molecule — a new atom of that element is placed at a chemically plausible, deterministic position (sp 180°, sp2 120°, sp3 ~109.47°; an allene-center Sp atom, whose two double-bonded neighbors are collinear, falls back to perpendicular to the multiple-bond axis) at the covalent-radii-sum bond length, bonded with the selected order, and committed as one undoable step with the full adjust-hydrogens choreography; different-element clicks keep the existing alchemy; three pre-existing stroke-state bugs (unguarded m_forceField derefs, early-return cleanup skips, lock-failure stale state) are fixed; the tooltip documents click/drag/right-click. Evidence: OpenSpec state=all_done (16/16 tasks); full suite 46/46 under Xvfb; placementtest 15/15; autooptreprotest 24/24 including three new live click-extend scenarios; Qt6 CI run 41993280536 success; Windows Installer run 41993280463 success. Tests: cmake --build build && ctest 46/46 pass; placementtest 15/15 pass; live autooptreprotest under Xvfb 24/24 pass. Unresolved: a pre-existing ChangeElementDrawCommand element-0 path on a jittered same-element click (reviewer finding 4) is rejected as out of scope — byte-identical to pre-change behavior, and a naive "fix" would regress the dummy-atom (element 0) alchemy case; the live GUI tests QSKIP under the offscreen ctest platform and run under Xvfb. Next: archive the change (openspec archive) when ready. — NOTE: low evidence density: no path:line evidence tokens and no verification gate rows — add file:line pointers (e.g. extensions/goal-recovery.ts:847) or a gateRows inventory so the terminal render is verifiable

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The DrawTool click-to-extend gesture (ChemDraw-style) is implemented, verified, and CI-green on both Linux (Qt6) and Windows (MSVC installer). Changed: clicking an atom of the currently-selected element now grows the molecule — a new atom of that element is placed at a chemically plausible, deterministic position (sp 180°, sp2 120°, sp3 ~109.47°; an allene-center Sp atom, whose two double-bonded neighbors are collinear, falls back to perpendicular to the multiple-bond axis) at the covalent-radii-sum bond length, bonded with the selected order, and committed as one undoable step with the full adjust-hydrogens choreography; different-element clicks keep the existing alchemy; three pre-existing stroke-state bugs (unguarded m_forceField derefs, early-return cleanup skips, lock-failure stale state) are fixed; the tooltip documents click/drag/right-click. Evidence: OpenSpec state=all_done (16/16 tasks); full suite 46/46 under Xvfb; placementtest 15/15; autooptreprotest 24/24 including three new live click-extend scenarios; Qt6 CI run 41993280536 success; Windows Installer run 41993280463 success. Tests: cmake --build build && ctest 46/46 pass; placementtest 15/15 pass; live autooptreprotest under Xvfb 24/24 pass. Unresolved: a pre-existing ChangeElementDrawCommand element-0 path on a jittered same-element click (reviewer finding 4) is rejected as out of scope — byte-identical to pre-change behavior, and a naive "fix" would regress the dummy-atom (element 0) alchemy case; the live GUI tests QSKIP under the offscreen ctest platform and run under Xvfb. Next: archive the change (openspec archive) when ready. — NOTE: low evidence density: no path:line evidence tokens and no verification gate rows — add file:line pointers (e.g. extensions/goal-recovery.ts:847) or a gateRows inventory so the terminal render is verifiable

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: The DrawTool click-to-extend gesture (ChemDraw-style) is implemented, verified, and CI-green on both Linux (Qt6) and Windows (MSVC installer). Changed: clicking an atom of the currently-selected element now grows the molecule — a new atom of that element is placed at a chemically plausible, deterministic position (sp 180°, sp2 120°, sp3 ~109.47°; an allene-center Sp atom, whose two double-bonded neighbors are collinear, falls back to perpendicular to the multiple-bond axis) at the covalent-radii-sum bond length, bonded with the selected order, and committed as one undoable step with the full adjust-hydrogens choreography; different-element clicks keep the existing alchemy; three pre-existing stroke-state bugs (unguarded m_forceField derefs, early-return cleanup skips, lock-failure stale state) are fixed; the tooltip documents click/drag/right-click. Evidence: OpenSpec state=all_done (16/16 tasks); full suite 46/46 under Xvfb; placementtest 15/15; autooptreprotest 24/24 including three new live click-extend scenarios; Qt6 CI run 41993280536 success; Windows Installer run 41993280463 success. Tests: cmake --build build && ctest 46/46 pass; placementtest 15/15 pass; live autooptreprotest under Xvfb 24/24 pass. Unresolved: a pre-existing ChangeElementDrawCommand element-0 path on a jittered same-element click (reviewer finding 4) is rejected as out of scope — byte-identical to pre-change behavior, and a naive "fix" would regress the dummy-atom (element 0) alchemy case; the live GUI tests QSKIP under the offscreen ctest platform and run under Xvfb. Next: archive the change (openspec archive) when ready. — NOTE: low evidence density: no path:line evidence tokens and no verification gate rows — add file:line pointers (e.g. extensions/goal-recovery.ts:847) or a gateRows inventory so the terminal render is verifiable

3. Build: `cmake --build build --parallel -j8` exit 0.
4. Full suite: `xvfb-run -a ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure -j8` -> 46/46 passed (100%).
5. Placement unit test: `./build/bin/placementtest` (offscreen) -> 15/15 passed.
6. Live gesture: `xvfb-run -a ./build/bin/autooptreprotest` (real xcb GL context) -> 24/24 passed, including the three new click-extend scenarios.
7. Qt6 CI on HEAD 87cbfe04f: run 41993280536 completed success (5/5 jobs).
8. Windows Installer CI on HEAD 87cbfe04f: run 41993280463 completed success (2/2 jobs).
9. Repository coherent: HEAD=87cbfe04f in sync with upstream; all source/OpenSpec changes committed and pushed.

Reviewer findings (5.4) disposition: Finding 1 (MAJOR, allene-center spec conformance) ACCEPT — perpendicular fallback + spec amendment + scenario/tests. Finding 2 (MINOR, design.md D2 signs) ACCEPT. Finding 3 (MINOR, missing n==2 Sp2/Sp tests) ACCEPT. Finding 4 (MINOR, pre-existing element-0 path) REJECT — out of scope, byte-identical to pre-change. Finding 5 (NIT, redundant clickBegin) ACCEPT-as-harmless. Finding 6 (NIT, lock-failure not clearing m_clickExtendCandidate) ACCEPT.

Changed: clicking an atom of the currently-selected element now grows the molecule — a new atom of that element is placed at a chemically plausible, deterministic position (sp 180°, sp2 120°, sp3 ~109.47°; an allene-center Sp atom, whose two double-bonded neighbors are collinear, falls back to perpendicular to the multiple-bond axis) at the covalent-radii-sum bond length, bonded with the selected order, and committed as one undoable step with the full adjust-hydrogens choreography; different-element clicks keep the existing alchemy; three pre-existing stroke-state bugs (unguarded m_forceField derefs, early-return cleanup skips, lock-failure stale state) are fixed; the tooltip documents click/drag/right-click. Changed: clicking an atom of the currently-selected element now grows the molecule — a new atom of that element is placed at a chemically plausible, deterministic position (sp 180°, sp2 120°, sp3 ~109.47°; an allene-center Sp atom, whose two double-bonded neighbors are collinear, falls back to perpendicular to the multiple-bond axis) at the covalent-radii-sum bond length, bonded with the selected order, and committed as one undoable step with the full adjust-hydrogens choreography; different-element clicks keep the existing alchemy; three pre-existing stroke-state bugs (unguarded m_forceField derefs, early-return cleanup skips, lock-failure stale state) are fixed; the tooltip documents click/drag/right-click. durableSolution.reason: The manual matrix (OpenSpec task 3.2) is a human visual verification step that cannot be executed in this headless environment. It requires a real display whose GL context resolves to a Compatibility profile so surface meshes render, plus human visual inspection of a wireframe net during a camera drag. Design D6 explicitly records this exact limitation. All automatable verification is complete and green.
durableSolution.durableFix: The manual matrix is not a code fix; it is a human verification step. The behavior is otherwise verified by the local build, the full 46-test suite (consumerparity + meshstream included), the reviewer confirmation, and both CI legs (Linux Qt6 CI and Windows Installer/MSVC). The durable follow-up is to run the manual matrix on a real Compatibility-profile display and confirm the spec-delta scenarios.
durableSolution.evidence: Verified empirically: Xvfb/llvmpipe resolves to Core profile (GL 4.5 Core) in avo2.log despite CompatibilityProfile request; coreFixedFunctionAvailable() returns false on Core so drawMesh/drawColorMesh bail and surfaces never render; a synthesized camera drag under Xvfb rotated the molecule (f0 vs f1 differ by 97353 px) but produced no surface render (f1 == f2, 0 px diff).

durableSolution.reason: The manual matrix (OpenSpec task 3.2) is a human visual verification step that cannot be executed in this headless environment. It requires a real display whose GL context resolves to a Compatibility profile so surface meshes render, plus human visual inspection of a wireframe net during a camera drag. Design D6 explicitly records this exact limitation. All automatable verification is complete and green.
durableSolution.durableFix: The manual matrix is not a code fix; it is a human verification step. The behavior is otherwise verified by the local build, the full 46-test suite (consumerparity + meshstream included), the reviewer confirmation, and both CI legs (Linux Qt6 CI and Windows Installer/MSVC). durableSolution.evidence: Verified empirically: Xvfb/llvmpipe resolves to Core profile (GL 4.5 Core) in avo2.log despite CompatibilityProfile request; coreFixedFunctionAvailable() returns false on Core so drawMesh/drawColorMesh bail and surfaces never render; a synthesized camera drag under Xvfb rotated the molecule (f0 vs f1 differ by 97353 px) but produced no surface render (f1 == f2, 0 px diff).
durableSolution.followUp: Run the OpenSpec task 3.2 manual matrix on a real display with a Compatibility-profile GL context: open testfiles/koffein_orca.out, display an ORCA orbital surface, tilt/rotate the camera, and confirm the surface stays visible as a wireframe net during the drag and returns to solid on release (no 250 ms blink). Also check the compat tier (AVOGADRO_RENDERER=compat) and an ESP-colored surface. Report which rows pass/fail.

blocker.evidence: Xvfb/llvmpipe resolves to Core profile (GL 4.5 Core) despite the app requesting CompatibilityProfile (main.cpp:216). GLPainterPrivate::coreFixedFunctionAvailable() (glpainter_p.cpp:282-300) returns false on a Core context, so drawMesh (glpainter_p.cpp:1341) and drawColorMesh (1408) early-return and surface meshes are never rendered. Verified empirically: a synthesized camera drag under Xvfb rotates the molecule (frame diff 97353 px) but no surface mesh is ever drawn. Design D6 records that offscreen/CI cannot drive real GLWidget mouse drags.

blocker.evidence: Xvfb/llvmpipe resolves to Core profile (GL 4.5 Core) despite the app requesting CompatibilityProfile (main.cpp:216). Verified empirically: a synthesized camera drag under Xvfb rotates the molecule (frame diff 97353 px) but no surface mesh is ever drawn. Design D6 records that offscreen/CI cannot drive real GLWidget mouse drags.

durableSolution.evidence: Verified empirically: Xvfb/llvmpipe resolves to Core profile (GL 4.5 Core) in avo2.log despite CompatibilityProfile request; coreFixedFunctionAvailable() returns false on Core so drawMesh/drawColorMesh bail and surfaces never render; a synthesized camera drag under Xvfb rotated the molecule (f0 vs f1 differ by 97353 px) but produced no surface render (f1 == f2, 0 px diff).
durableSolution.followUp: Run the OpenSpec task 3.2 manual matrix on a real display with a Compatibility-profile GL context: open testfiles/koffein_orca.out, display an ORCA orbital surface, tilt/rotate the camera, and confirm the surface stays visible as a wireframe net during the drag and returns to solid on release (no 250 ms blink). Also check the compat tier (AVOGADRO_RENDERER=compat) and an ESP-colored surface. Report which rows pass/fail.

blocker.evidence: Xvfb/llvmpipe resolves to Core profile (GL 4.5 Core) despite the app requesting CompatibilityProfile (main.cpp:216). GLPainterPrivate::coreFixedFunctionAvailable() (glpainter_p.cpp:282-300) returns false on a Core context, so drawMesh (glpainter_p.cpp:1341) and drawColorMesh (1408) early-return and surface meshes are never rendered. Verified empirically: a synthesized camera drag under Xvfb rotates the molecule (frame diff 97353 px) but no surface mesh is ever drawn. Design D6 records that offscreen/CI cannot drive real GLWidget mouse drags.

blocker.evidence: Xvfb/llvmpipe resolves to Core profile (GL 4.5 Core) despite the app requesting CompatibilityProfile (main.cpp:216). Verified empirically: a synthesized camera drag under Xvfb rotates the molecule (frame diff 97353 px) but no surface mesh is ever drawn. Design D6 records that offscreen/CI cannot drive real GLWidget mouse drags.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

Fixed-angle drag (2px move) isolates the wireframe toggle from camera rotation: modern tier interior_ratio 0.916 (solid) -> 0.640 (wireframe during drag) -> 0.917 (solid after release); compat tier 0.918 -> 0.576 -> 0.917. pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

All 6 OpenSpec tasks are checked; the GLLA task mirror is fully complete. Code change (glwidget.cpp/glwidget.h) committed as 4cc64e4d0 and pushed; OpenSpec task-completion docs committed as d9a307076 and pushed. Working tree clean except for GLLA/project state files (.pi-glla/, .pi/, goal-revisions.json), which are not part of the change. CI: both Windows/MSVC installer legs and Linux Qt6 legs pass for commit 4cc64e4d0 (verified prior). Manual matrix executed: app launched under Xvfb :99 with MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT (resolves Compatibility profile; renderer tier modern/compat), xfwm4 window manager running, testfiles/koffein_orca.out loaded, orbital row selected from the Orbitals dock so a surface displayed, camera drags driven via xdotool. Fixed-angle drag (2px move) isolates the wireframe toggle from camera rotation: modern tier interior_ratio 0.916 (solid) -> 0.640 (wireframe during drag) -> 0.917 (solid after release); compat tier 0.918 -> 0.576 -> 0.917. Continuous 8-step drag: surface present in every frame (colored pixels 48552-86685, never 0). At-rest rendering unchanged (flushMode == inst.mode when not interacting).

findings: Surfaces render as a wireframe net during camera drags and return to solid on release — modern tier fixed-angle test: interior_ratio 0.916 (solid) → 0.640 (wireframe) → 0.917 (solid); colored pixels 60721 → 48125 → 61344
Compat tier shows the same behavior — interior_ratio 0.918 → 0.576 → 0.917; colored pixels 90169 → 62739 → 90083
No frame presents the molecule without the surface during a continuous drag — surface present in all 8 captured frames (colored pixels 48552–86685, never 0)

findings: ESP-colored surfaces draw via drawColorMesh; the reviewer confirmed drawColorMesh implements mode 1 (GL_LINE, lighting off, per-vertex colors preserved), so the same flushMode substitution applies — verified by shared code path, not by generating an ESP mesh through the surfaces dialog headlessly
Mid-drag surface recalculation is pre-existing unchanged behavior — the stability skip and try-lock skip are untouched (reviewer checkpoints 1–2)
tests: Reviewer checkpoint 4 (flushMode reduces to inst.mode when not interacting) — PASS

blocker.evidence: Xvfb/llvmpipe resolves to Core profile (GL 4.5 Core) despite the app requesting CompatibilityProfile (main.cpp:216). GLPainterPrivate::coreFixedFunctionAvailable() (glpainter_p.cpp:282-300) returns false on a Core context, so drawMesh (glpainter_p.cpp:1341) and drawColorMesh (1408) early-return and surface meshes are never rendered. Verified empirically: a synthesized camera drag under Xvfb rotates the molecule (frame diff 97353 px) but no surface mesh is ever drawn. Design D6 records that offscreen/CI cannot drive real GLWidget mouse drags.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

Working tree clean except for GLLA/project state files (.pi-glla/, .pi/, goal-revisions.json), which are not part of the change. CI: both Windows/MSVC installer legs and Linux Qt6 legs pass for commit 4cc64e4d0 (verified prior). Manual matrix executed: app launched under Xvfb :99 with MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT (resolves Compatibility profile; renderer tier modern/compat), xfwm4 window manager running, testfiles/koffein_orca.out loaded, orbital row selected from the Orbitals dock so a surface displayed, camera drags driven via xdotool. Fixed-angle drag (2px move) isolates the wireframe toggle from camera rotation: modern tier interior_ratio 0.916 (solid) -> 0.640 (wireframe during drag) -> 0.917 (solid after release); compat tier 0.918 -> 0.576 -> 0.917. Continuous 8-step drag: surface present in every frame (colored pixels 48552-86685, never 0). At-rest rendering unchanged (flushMode == inst.mode when not interacting).

findings: Surfaces render as a wireframe net during camera drags and return to solid on release — modern tier fixed-angle test: interior_ratio 0.916 (solid) → 0.640 (wireframe) → 0.917 (solid); colored pixels 60721 → 48125 → 61344

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.

Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.

Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.

Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

durableSolution.followUp: Run the OpenSpec task 3.2 manual matrix on a real display with a Compatibility-profile GL context: open testfiles/koffein_orca.out, display an ORCA orbital surface, tilt/rotate the camera, and confirm the surface stays visible as a wireframe net during the drag and returns to solid on release (no 250 ms blink). Also check the compat tier (AVOGADRO_RENDERER=compat) and an ESP-colored surface. Report which rows pass/fail.

blocker.evidence: Xvfb/llvmpipe resolves to Core profile (GL 4.5 Core) despite the app requesting CompatibilityProfile (main.cpp:216). GLPainterPrivate::coreFixedFunctionAvailable() (glpainter_p.cpp:282-300) returns false on a Core context, so drawMesh (glpainter_p.cpp:1341) and drawColorMesh (1408) early-return and surface meshes are never rendered. Verified empirically: a synthesized camera drag under Xvfb rotates the molecule (frame diff 97353 px) but no surface mesh is ever drawn. Design D6 records that offscreen/CI cannot drive real GLWidget mouse drags.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: OpenSpec status --change fix-surface-drag-wireframe --json returns isPlanningComplete=True and isComplete=True. openspec instructions apply --change fix-surface-drag-wireframe --json returns state="all_done". All 6 OpenSpec tasks are checked; the GLLA task mirror is fully complete. Code change (glwidget.cpp/glwidget.h) committed as 4cc64e4d0 and pushed; OpenSpec task-completion docs committed as d9a307076 and pushed. Working tree clean except for GLLA/project state files (.pi-glla/, .pi/, goal-revisions.json), which are not part of the change. CI: both Windows/MSVC installer legs and Linux Qt6 legs pass for commit 4cc64e4d0 (verified prior). Manual matrix executed: app launched under Xvfb :99 with MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT (resolves Compatibility profile; renderer tier modern/compat), xfwm4 window manager running, testfiles/koffein_orca.out loaded, orbital row selected from the Orbitals dock so a surface displayed, camera drags driven via xdotool. Fixed-angle drag (2px move) isolates the wireframe toggle from camera rotation: modern tier interior_ratio 0.916 (solid) -> 0.640 (wireframe during drag) -> 0.917 (solid after release); compat tier 0.918 -> 0.576 -> 0.917. Continuous 8-step drag: surface present in every frame (colored pixels 48552-86685, never 0). At-rest rendering unchanged (flushMode == inst.mode when not interacting).

findingGroups.title: Manual matrix under Xvfb + llvmpipe (Compatibility context)
findings: Surfaces render as a wireframe net during camera drags and return to solid on release — modern tier fixed-angle test: interior_ratio 0.916 (solid) → 0.640 (wireframe) → 0.917 (solid); colored pixels 60721 → 48125 → 61344
Compat tier shows the same behavior — interior_ratio 0.918 → 0.576 → 0.917; colored pixels 90169 → 62739 → 90083
No frame presents the molecule without the surface during a continuous drag — surface present in all 8 captured frames (colored pixels 48552–86685, never 0)
At-rest rendering is byte-identical to pre-change — flushMode == inst.mode when not interacting (reviewer checkpoint 4); surface renders solid at rest (interior_ratio ~0.92)
Verification was enabled by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT) with a running window manager (xfwm4), which the earlier Core-profile attempt could not do

findingGroups.title: ESP surface row (3) and mid-drag recalculation row (6)
findings: ESP-colored surfaces draw via drawColorMesh; the reviewer confirmed drawColorMesh implements mode 1 (GL_LINE, lighting off, per-vertex colors preserved), so the same flushMode substitution applies — verified by shared code path, not by generating an ESP mesh through the surfaces dialog headlessly
Mid-drag surface recalculation is pre-existing unchanged behavior — the stability skip and try-lock skip are untouched (reviewer checkpoints 1–2)
tests: Reviewer checkpoint 4 (flushMode reduces to inst.mode when not interacting) — PASS
Reviewer checkpoint 5 (drawMesh and drawColorMesh both implement mode 1) — PASS
